clue.text: Partially undress — start to get between the sheets to retire

indicators.note: to retire is to go back, so the assembled letters are read backwards
the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: someone between the sheets is in bed, abed

explanation.surface: A drowsy person half-strips before slipping under the covers for the night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'between' looks like a container signal but is part of the phrase for ABED; 'to retire' turns G + ABED into DEBAG. DEBAG is old schoolboy slang for pulling someone's trousers off.
explanation.definitionFit: To debag is to remove a person's trousers, a partial stripping usually done as a prank.

clue.text: Came into existence, died, and was shrouded, without a name

indicators.note: without means losing the named letter

parts.note: enveloped means covered or shrouded

explanation.surface: A grim life story: born, dead and wrapped in an anonymous shroud.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that developed grew and emerged into being.

clue.text: Statesman once saved from perilous situation

definitions.meaning: Francis ... was Lord Chancellor under James I
to save one's ... is to escape from danger

explanation.definitionFit: Francis Bacon was an Elizabethan and Jacobean statesman; and the idiom 'save your bacon' means rescue yourself from trouble.

clue.text: Fail with issue

definitions.meaning: to stop working, as an engine might

explanation.definitionFit: An engine can stop working, and an official can distribute leaflets: both are the same phrasal verb.

clue.text: To live by compiling is tempting

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
compiling a crossword is setting it

explanation.surface: A crossword setter confesses that making puzzles for a living is a constant temptation.
explanation.definitionFit: A besetting sin is one that constantly assails or tempts a person.

clue.text: It held so many sweeps it needed two banks

definitions.text: It held so many sweeps it needed two banks

parts.words: It held so many sweeps it needed two banks
parts.note: suggests chimney sweeps and money banks, but the sweeps are long oars and the banks are tiers of rowers

explanation.definitionFit: An ancient galley with two tiers of oars on each side.

clue.text: The way to bear the expense of a county town

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
to afford something is to be able to pay for it

explanation.surface: A traveller wonders how to pay for the road to a provincial capital.
explanation.walkthrough: STAFFORD is the county town (administrative centre) of Staffordshire in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Stafford is the administrative centre of Staffordshire, an English county.

clue.text: Mad Hatter steps on the Dormouse's tail — such drama

indicators.note: mad suggests the letters are deranged and rearranged
a tail is the last letter of a word

explanation.surface: At Alice's tea party the Hatter treads on the sleepy Dormouse, causing a scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad Hatter' reads as the Wonderland character, but 'Mad' rearranges HATTER to THEATR; the E is the Dormouse's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre is dramatic art, plays as a genre.

clue.text: Having trouble finding place for stock

definitions.meaning: literally located in broth, where stock is used

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means being in difficulties; and soup is where a cook's stock ends up.

clue.text: Nebuchadnezzar ate this peach

definitions.meaning: in the Book of Daniel the Babylonian king was driven out to eat like an ox
to peach is to inform on someone

explanation.definitionFit: The Bible says King Nebuchadnezzar ate herbage like oxen; and to peach on someone is to inform, British slang for which is the same word.

clue.text: Boy always had attraction for exact opposite

definitions.text: Boy always had attraction for exact opposite

parts.words: Boy always had attraction for exact opposite
parts.note: the title of F. Anstey's comic novel in which a boy and his father swap bodies, each becoming the other, the phrase also meaning the reverse case

explanation.walkthrough: The clue alludes to a Victorian novel where schoolboy and father exchange places, while the Latin tag itself means 'the other way round'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin tag means 'the order being reversed', the exact opposite of what was just said.

clue.text: Run over

definitions.meaning: in cricket a run not scored off the bat, such as a bye or wide, is added to the total separately

explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a bye or wide is a run added to the score; and anything left over is surplus or additional.

clue.text: Get masterly hand-off, playing for Wales

indicators.note: playing about with the letters of the rugby phrase rearranges them

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rugby player executes a superb hand-off in a match for the Welsh side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get' is a link word; 'playing' rearranges MASTERLY HAND-OFF. The anthem is played for Wales before rugby internationals, where a hand-off fends off a tackler.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh national anthem, sung before Wales rugby internationals, is titled in English with these words.

clue.text: Wearing a jacket for dinner?

parts.note: suggests a man in formal dress at a dinner party, but the thing in its jacket is a baked tuber served to eat

explanation.definitionFit: A baked spud cooked in its skin is called a jacket one, and it is eaten at dinner.

clue.text: Marked flyer moving right to me

indicators.note: moving the letters around rearranges them

explanation.surface: A striped insect flies off to the right towards the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: This moth has bold striped wings, and is also a famous biplane, both flying things.

clue.text: Bonus for drinkers in Singapore, for example

parts.note: a bonus comes free of charge
port is a fortified wine for drinkers

explanation.surface: Customers in a Singapore bar get a complimentary round as a special bonus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word; Singapore is a famous duty-free trading harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Singapore is a well-known example of a harbour where goods are traded without customs duties.

clue.text: When bones break this one's left without compensation

indicators.note: break means the bones split the remaining letters open
has left means the one has gone, removing it

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral; one's means one has
ankles are joints of bones

explanation.surface: Someone whose bones break is left uncompensated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's left' reads as 'one has left': I leaves THIS to give THS, which ANKLES breaks into.
explanation.definitionFit: A thankless job brings no reward or gratitude.

clue.text: Detailed act oppresses church, giving no option

indicators.note: in a down clue oppresses means sitting on top of the later piece
detailed means with the tail cut off, removing the last letter

parts.note: to perform is to act
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A harsh law that bears down on the church leaves it no choice.
explanation.definitionFit: Perforce means of necessity, unavoidably, with no choice.

clue.text: Republican leader with a colour to be worn

parts.note: the Doge was the elected leader of the republics of Venice and Genoa
red is a colour

explanation.surface: A party politician turns up sporting a coloured rosette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Republican' suggests a US party, but the leader is the Doge of the Venetian Republic.
explanation.definitionFit: A book with folded-down page corners is shabby from use, hence worn.

clue.text: Brutish men hit hard in a rising

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards

parts.note: to slam is to hit hard

explanation.surface: Thugs beat people up during an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals are brutes, men behaving with bestial cruelty.

clue.text: After housework, note, there's amusement

indicators.note: after places the note behind the earlier letters

parts.note: split as house, HO, and work, OP (opus)
la is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Once the cleaning is done, a memo announces it is time for some fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'housework' must be split: HO is the abbreviation for house, and OP for a musical work.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoopla is a fairground game of throwing rings over prizes, an entertainment.

clue.text: Find routes off to the south for heat

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Someone plans roads heading south to escape the hot weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Oestrus is the period when a female mammal is on heat, sexually receptive.

clue.text: Part of the body very exposed, after an article slips down?

indicators.note: in a down clue slipping down means moving lower in the word

parts.note: barest is the most exposed, very bare
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A wardrobe malfunction leaves someone revealed when a garment slips.
explanation.definitionFit: The chest is part of the torso.

clue.text: Arena where wit provided rural community with a little excitement?

parts.note: a card is a witty, amusing person
provided that means if
a farm is a rural establishment
a spark is a little flash of life or excitement

explanation.surface: A joker brings a bit of fun to a sleepy village.
explanation.walkthrough: CARDIFF ARMS PARK is the historic rugby stadium in Cardiff, the Welsh capital.
explanation.definitionFit: This Welsh rugby ground is a sports stadium, a venue for games.

clue.text: Vegetable sounds burnt

indicators.note: sounds means the word is heard as another

parts.note: charred means scorched or burnt

explanation.surface: Someone says the greens on the stove smell burnt.
explanation.definitionFit: Swiss chard is a leafy green eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: No particular number in trouble

parts.note: any means no particular one

explanation.surface: A vague count of people are in difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: To annoy is to bother or irritate.

clue.text: Siler and gold find a market, classically

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Precious metals are taken to be sold in a market.
explanation.definitionFit: An agora was the public square and marketplace of an ancient Greek city.

clue.text: Give a new order and soldiers are called in

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: rang means telephoned or called

explanation.surface: A commanding officer issues fresh instructions and summons the troops.
explanation.definitionFit: To rearrange is to put things in a different sequence or arrangement.

clue.text: Generous about a chap's popping out

indicators.note: about means going round the other piece

parts.note: decent can mean generous, as in a decent helping
belonging to a man, his

explanation.surface: A kindly man is just nipping out for a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically, a seed pod that is dehiscent bursts open to release its seeds.

clue.text: Do they upset viewers, in a way? That's right

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
yes is an affirmation that something is right

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether certain shows disturb the audience, and is told that is correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'viewers' sounds like an audience, but means eyes, which these swellings irritate.
explanation.definitionFit: Sties are inflamed swellings on the eyelid, which trouble the eyes.
